goals.description: If elevated blood pressure is present, confirm it using at least two measurements on separate occasions.

Complete the elevated-blood-pressure baseline assessment: review prescription and over-the-counter medications, document diabetes and kidney disease assessment, and obtain a baseline basic metabolic panel.

Determine treatment eligibility from office systolic blood pressure and documented comorbidities, discuss options with the patient, and implement the applicable Table 1 treatment and follow-up. Diabetes is documented; the source medication threshold for this patient is SBP >=130 mmHg. No medication order can be generated until the missing clinical inputs and medication route are verified.
Adopt a DASH dietary pattern and keep daily sodium intake strictly below 2300 mg.
Perform at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week OR at least 75 minutes of vigorous-intensity aerobic activity per week.

Achieve and maintain BMI within 18.5-24.9 kg/m2. Baseline BMI is unknown; do not presume that weight loss is indicated. If weight loss is clinically appropriate, discuss the source-described blood-pressure benefit of a 5-10% reduction.

If alcohol is consumed, stay within the verified guideline alcohol category limit: no more than 2 drinks/day for the guideline's men category or 1 drink/day for its women category. Category and current intake remain unresolved; no patient-specific category is assigned from demographic gender alone.
If smoking is present, provide smoking cessation counseling and resources to support cessation.

After a Table 1 treatment decision, obtain home blood pressure readings twice each morning and twice each evening on at least 3, preferably 7, consecutive days and submit readings weekly. Review weekly averages and complete each submission review within 7 days.
During home monitoring, send a reminder after a week without readings and make direct contact to assess barriers after 3 reminder attempts on different days without receipt of readings.

Review the seven-day home blood pressure average 2-4 weeks after medication initiation or change. For lifestyle-only management, review home readings at the applicable Table 1 follow-up visit. Keep this review distinct from laboratory follow-up and weekly submission review.
If treatment initiation criteria are met, document receipt of appropriate pharmacotherapy within 30 days of meeting those criteria.

If ACE inhibitor therapy is used, document whether required follow-up laboratory monitoring was completed within the source-recommended timeframe. The timeframe must be obtained before a laboratory schedule or measure result can be generated.

activities.description: If elevated blood pressure is present, confirm blood pressure with at least two measurements on separate occasions and document office systolic and diastolic values and measurement occasions.
activities.frequency: At least two measurements on separate occasions during assessment of elevated blood pressure; spacing between occasions is not specified.
activities.clinicalRationale: The confirmation decision failed because the number of measurement occasions is missing; classification and treatment decisions also lack office blood pressure. The existing diagnosis does not establish a current blood pressure value. The annual documentation model reports denominator-only membership, but no separate annual-documentation recommendation was supplied.

activities.description: For the elevated-blood-pressure baseline assessment, obtain a basic metabolic panel and assess diabetes and chronic kidney disease status. Record the supplied type 2 diabetes diagnosis; verify kidney disease status rather than treating an inventory miss as confirmed absence.
activities.frequency: Once at baseline during assessment of elevated blood pressure.
activities.clinicalRationale: Baseline laboratory and comorbidity assessment support treatment selection and subsequent monitoring. Diabetes is documented, but no laboratory results or confirmed kidney assessment are supplied.

activities.description: Review and reconcile the current medication list, including over-the-counter products, during the elevated-blood-pressure assessment.
activities.frequency: During the assessment of elevated blood pressure.
activities.clinicalRationale: No medication list is provided; current treatment cannot be inferred from failed decision evaluations or inventory misses.

activities.description: Complete clinician review of the single source regimen, lisinopril 10 mg daily, without generating a medication order. With documented diabetes, Table 1 specifies this regimen if office SBP is >=130 mmHg, with or without kidney disease, and treatment follow-up in 2 weeks. The same source also directs pharmacotherapy at SBP >=140 mmHg regardless of comorbidity. If SBP is <130 mmHg, the source narrative directs lifestyle management and 12-week follow-up; the table explicitly includes diabetes without kidney disease in that branch but does not provide a row for both diabetes and kidney disease at SBP <130 mmHg. Verify current BP, kidney status, current therapy, and the missing medication route before generating an executable regimen. Preserve both source recommendations as one identical-regimen candidate.
activities.clinicalRationale: The treatment decision failed because office SBP is missing, so no treatment branch was selected. Both recommendations describe the same drug, dose, and frequency; neither provides a route. A process review preserves the recommendation without inventing a route or issuing an incomplete medication activity. The guideline-applicability decision also failed because its Age input was missing.

activities.description: Explain the documented hypertension diagnosis, current blood pressure results when available, and applicable treatment options; involve the patient in shared treatment decisions.
activities.frequency: During treatment decision-making; no recurring interval is specified.
activities.clinicalRationale: Shared decision-making is recommended independently of which treatment branch is ultimately selected. Current blood pressure control is unknown.

activities.description: Use verified blood pressure and documented comorbidities in EHR decision support. Notify the clinician when pharmacotherapy criteria are met; for this patient with diabetes, the source threshold is office SBP >=130 mmHg. Do not interpret empty or failed decision outputs as an eligibility result.
activities.frequency: When verified decision inputs establish pharmacotherapy eligibility.
activities.clinicalRationale: Diabetes lowers the source treatment threshold, but office SBP is absent and the treatment model returned an error rather than a recommendation.

activities.description: Counsel the patient to adopt the DASH diet: choose fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy products; limit saturated fat; and keep sodium intake strictly below 2300 mg each day.
activities.frequency: Daily dietary pattern; counseling interval is not specified.
activities.clinicalRationale: Lifestyle counseling applies to all patients with hypertension. The sodium assessment failed because intake is missing; counseling is supported, but excessive current intake cannot be assumed.

activities.description: Counsel the patient to perform at least 150 minutes per week of moderate aerobic exercise, such as brisk walking, OR at least 75 minutes per week of vigorous aerobic exercise.
activities.frequency: Weekly activity totals: >=150 minutes moderate OR >=75 minutes vigorous.
activities.clinicalRationale: The activity target is recommended for hypertension regardless of medication use. Missing baseline activity caused decision failure and does not establish inactivity.

activities.description: Counsel on achieving or maintaining BMI 18.5-24.9 kg/m2 through the recommended DASH dietary pattern and aerobic activity. Establish current weight status before recommending weight reduction; when reduction is appropriate, discuss the source-described benefit of 5-10% weight loss.
activities.frequency: Ongoing weight-management behavior; no assessment or counseling interval is specified.
activities.clinicalRationale: The BMI model failed because BMI is missing. The healthy-weight target is supported, but overweight status and a patient-specific weight-loss target are not established.

activities.description: Clarify current alcohol intake and the applicable guideline alcohol category. If alcohol is consumed, counsel on no more than 2 drinks/day for the guideline's men category or 1 drink/day for its women category. Do not assign a category or imply current alcohol use from the supplied demographic data.
activities.frequency: Daily intake ceiling once the applicable category is verified.
activities.clinicalRationale: The alcohol model failed because category and daily intake are missing. Its hypertension=false input conflicts with the supplied hypertension diagnoses and requires correction before reevaluation.

activities.description: Establish whether smoking cessation support applies. If the patient smokes, provide cessation counseling and resources to help stop smoking.
activities.frequency: If smoking is present; no recurring interval is specified.
activities.clinicalRationale: The recommendation is conditional and smoking status is not supplied.

activities.description: After a Table 1 treatment decision has been made, measure home systolic and diastolic blood pressure with a validated upper-arm device. Take two readings one minute apart in the morning before medications and two readings one minute apart in the evening on at least three, preferably seven, consecutive days. Submit readings through the patient portal, secure messaging, or telephone each week.
activities.frequency: Two morning and two evening readings, one minute apart within each pair, on at least 3 and preferably 7 consecutive days; submit weekly.
activities.clinicalRationale: Home monitoring is recommended after a Table 1 treatment decision. The treatment decision is currently unresolved, so this activity remains conditional rather than an assertion that home monitoring has begun.

activities.description: For submitted home readings, review weekly average systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Notify the responsible clinician if average systolic BP is >=135 mmHg or average diastolic BP is >=85 mmHg, or if the average exceeds a lower threshold explicitly set by the clinician for diabetes or kidney disease. Do not invent a lower diabetes threshold.
activities.frequency: Weekly review of home blood pressure averages.
activities.clinicalRationale: The source equates a home average of 135/85 mmHg with an office reading of 140/90 mmHg and defines a notification trigger, not a patient-specific treatment goal.

activities.description: Track submission and review timestamps for weekly home blood pressure readings and record whether each submission was reviewed by the care team within seven days.
activities.frequency: For each weekly submission; review within 7 days of submission.
activities.clinicalRationale: The quality recommendation defines a seven-day review window independent of treatment-change follow-up and laboratory follow-up.

activities.description: During home monitoring, send a reminder if one week passes without readings. Track reminder attempts on different days. After three such attempts without receipt of readings, contact the patient directly to identify monitoring barriers. Verify elapsed absence and prior attempts before choosing the current outreach step.
activities.frequency: Reminder after 1 week without readings; direct contact after 3 reminder attempts on different days without readings. Exact spacing of reminder days is not specified.
activities.clinicalRationale: The missing-readings decision failed because reminder count is missing. The separate follow-up-timing model also lacks absence duration and distinct reminder days. Neither failed model establishes that direct-contact criteria have been met.
